questions.question:
**Fill in the blanks:**

In Carnatic music, a laghu with five beats is known as ____ jaati.
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**Khanda Jaati**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In **Carnatic music**, rhythm plays a vital role, and it is structured using various rhythmic cycles called **talas**.
 
• A **laghu** is a rhythmic unit within a tala, and its beat count is determined by the **jaati**.
 
• The term **Khanda Jaati** refers to a laghu with **five beats**.
 
• In the Khanda Jaati, the rhythmic pattern consists of five syllables or beats, which can be represented as **ta ka ta ki ta**.
 
• This is one of the five types of **jaatis** in Carnatic music, which include **Tishra (3 beats), Chaturashra (4 beats), Khanda (5 beats), Mishra (7 beats), and Sankeerna (9 beats)**.
 
• The usage of Khanda Jaati in talas adds complexity and richness to the rhythmic structure, showcasing the intricacy of **South Indian classical music**.
 
• Khanda Jaati is often employed in compositions to create distinctive and challenging rhythmic patterns that test the skill of performers.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Tishra Jaati**__

 __
 
• **Tishra Jaati** consists of **three beats** in the laghu.
 
• This jaati is represented as **ta ki ta**.
 
• It is one of the simplest jaatis and is widely used in basic rhythmic compositions in Carnatic music.
 
 
 
• **Chaturashra Jaati**__
 __
 
• **Chaturashra Jaati** consists of **four beats** in the laghu.
 
• The rhythmic pattern for Chaturashra Jaati is **ta ka di mi**.
 
• This is the most common jaati in Carnatic music and serves as the foundation for many talas.
 
 
 
• **Mishra Jaati**__
 
 
• **Mishra Jaati** consists of **seven beats** in the laghu.
 
• The rhythmic syllables are represented as **ta ki ta ta ka di mi**.
 
• This jaati is more intricate and is used to add complexity to compositions.

questions.question: Which of the following statements about Judo is **correct**?

options.text: Judo was introduced in 1882 by Jigoro Kano in Japan.
India's first National Judo Championship was held in 1970 at Delhi University.
Kalpana Devi won gold at the 2010 Judo World Cup.
Judo became an Olympic sport in 1965.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Judo was introduced in 1882 by Jigoro Kano in Japan**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Judo** is a modern Japanese martial art and combat sport that was created in **1882** by **Jigoro Kano**.
 
• The term **Judo** translates to "the gentle way" in Japanese.
 
• Kano founded the **Kodokan Judo Institute** in Japan, where he developed and taught this martial art.
 
• Judo focuses on techniques like **grappling, joint locks, chokeholds, and throws**, making it distinct from other martial arts that emphasize striking.
 
• It is based on principles like **"maximum efficiency with minimum effort"** and **"mutual welfare and benefit"**.
 
• Kano’s Judo emphasized physical education, self-defense, and moral development, which contributed to its recognition worldwide.
 
• Judo has become a **global sport** and is practiced in numerous countries, with competitions held at national and international levels.
 
• It became an **Olympic sport** for men in **1964** (Tokyo Olympics) and for women in **1992** (Barcelona Olympics).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **India's first National Judo Championship**__

 __
 
• The first National Judo Championship in India was held in **1970** at **Delhi University**. This event marked the formal recognition and organization of Judo as a sport in India.
 
• While this is a significant milestone in the history of Judo in India, it is not the correct answer as the question focuses on Judo's origins.
 
 
 
• **Kalpana Devi and the 2010 Judo World Cup**__
 __
 
• **Kalpana Devi** is a renowned Indian judoka who has represented India in various international competitions.
 
• However, she did not win the **gold medal** at the 2010 Judo World Cup. This statement is factually incorrect.
 
 
 
• **Judo as an Olympic sport**__
 
 
• Judo became an official **Olympic sport** in the year **1964** at the Tokyo Olympics, not in 1965 as stated in the option.
 
• The inclusion of Judo in the Olympics was a significant step in its international recognition.

Consider the following statements about glacial landforms:

**Statement 1: **Hanging valleys are often found opening into main glacial valleys at higher elevations.

**Statement 2:** Spurs of such hanging valleys are frequently truncated into triangular facets.

Which of the following Statements is/are **Correct**?
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**1 and 2 are correct**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Hanging valleys** are formed by tributary glaciers that join the main glacier at a higher elevation. This happens because the main glacier erodes deeper and more extensively than the tributary glacier.
 
• These valleys often open into **main glacial valleys** at a higher elevation, appearing as steep cliffs or waterfalls after the ice melts.
 
• The **spurs** of such hanging valleys are truncated into **triangular facets** due to glacial erosion. This truncation occurs as the glacier carves through the valley, cutting across the spurs and leaving behind triangular landforms.
 
• Hanging valleys are commonly associated with **waterfalls**, as the streams from the tributary valleys flow down into the main valley after the ice melts. A notable example is the **Yosemite Valley** in the United States.
 
• The processes involved in the formation of hanging valleys and triangular facets are examples of how glaciers reshape landscapes through both **erosion and deposition**.
 
• These features provide key evidence of the **intensity and direction of glacial movement** in an area, helping researchers understand past glacial environments.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Glacial Landforms**__

 
 
• Glaciers create various landforms through **erosion, transportation, and deposition**. These include features like cirques, horns, aretes, U-shaped valleys, and moraines.
 
• The study of glacial landforms helps in understanding **climatic changes** and the extent of glacial advances and retreats during the Earth's history.
 
• Glacial erosion processes like **plucking** and **abrasion** are responsible for the characteristic shape of valleys and other landforms.

questions.question: Which pathway in cellular respiration generates the most ATP?
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**Electron Transport Chain**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **electron transport chain (ETC)** is a crucial pathway in cellular respiration that generates the most **ATP (adenosine triphosphate).**
 
• It occurs in the inner membrane of the **mitochondria** in eukaryotic cells.
 
• The ETC uses high-energy electrons from molecules like **NADH and FADH₂**, which are produced during earlier stages of respiration.
 
• Electrons are transferred through a series of protein complexes, including **cytochromes**, which pump **protons (H⁺)** across the mitochondrial membrane, creating a **proton gradient.**
 
• This proton gradient powers the enzyme **ATP synthase** to synthesize ATP via a process called **oxidative phosphorylation.**
 
• The ETC is responsible for producing approximately **34 ATP molecules** per glucose molecule, making it the most efficient pathway in energy production.
 
• Oxygen acts as the final electron acceptor in the ETC, combining with protons and electrons to form **water**, which is essential to the process.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Glycolysis**__

 __
 
• **Glycolysis** is the first step in cellular respiration, occurring in the **cytoplasm** of the cell.
 
• It breaks down **glucose** into two molecules of **pyruvate**, producing a net gain of **2 ATP** molecules and **2 NADH** molecules.
 
• Though it is an essential step, it generates far less ATP compared to the ETC.
 
 
 
• **Krebs Cycle**__
 __
 
• The **Krebs cycle**, also known as the **citric acid cycle**, occurs in the mitochondrial matrix.
 
• It produces **NADH** and **FADH₂**, which are used in the electron transport chain.
 
• The cycle directly generates only **2 ATP** molecules per glucose molecule.
 
 
 
• **Fermentation**__
 
 
• **Fermentation** is an anaerobic process that occurs in the absence of oxygen.
 
• It produces ATP through **glycolysis** and regenerates **NAD+** for continued glycolysis.
 
• However, it generates only **2 ATP** molecules per glucose molecule, making it far less efficient than aerobic respiration.

questions.question: Which of the following most **accurately **describes the legal character of the right to property under Article 300A of the Indian Constitution?

options.text: It is a fundamental right that guarantees compensation for all property acquisitions.
It allows the State to deprive a person of property by any law, even without due process.
It is a constitutional legal right that permits deprivation only by authority of law.
It permits citizens to claim property protection under Article 32 before the Supreme Court.

questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**It is a constitutional legal right that permits deprivation only by authority of law.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Under **Article 300A** of the **Indian Constitution**, the right to property is no longer a **fundamental right**. It was demoted to a constitutional legal right by the **44th Constitutional Amendment Act, 1978.**
 
• This article states that no person shall be deprived of their property except by the **authority of law.**
 
• This ensures that property can only be taken by the state through a legally established process, providing protection against arbitrary deprivation.
 
• As a constitutional legal right, this provision primarily ensures that property rights are safeguarded as long as the deprivation occurs through proper legislation.
 
• Unlike fundamental rights, violations of Article 300A cannot be directly challenged under **Article 32** in the **Supreme Court**.
 
• However, if property is taken away without following the due process of law, remedies can be sought through the **High Courts under Article 226** or other legal avenues.
 
• The transformation of the right to property from fundamental to constitutional legal right reflects the state's ability to regulate property for public welfare, subject to legal procedures.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **It is a fundamental right that guarantees compensation for all property acquisitions.**__

 __
 
• Before the **44th Amendment Act**, the right to property was a fundamental right under **Articles 19(1)(f)** and **31**. However, post-amendment, Article 300A does not guarantee compensation for all acquisitions, and the right to property is now a constitutional legal right.
 
 
 
• **It allows the State to deprive a person of property by any law, even without due process.**__
 __
 
• This statement is incorrect as Article 300A explicitly requires deprivation to occur through the **authority of law**. Arbitrary deprivation without legal procedures violates the article.
 
 
 
• **It permits citizens to claim property protection under Article 32 before the Supreme Court.**__
 
 
• Property rights under Article 300A cannot be enforced through **Article 32**, as they are not fundamental rights. Remedies for violations must be sought through **High Courts under Article 226** or other legal mechanisms.

questions.question: For a rigid body, the angular velocity of any particle about a given axis of rotation is:

options.text: Proportional to its distance from the axis
Inversely proportional to its distance from the axis

questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**The same for all particles**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In a **rigid body**, all particles are fixed relative to each other and move collectively during rotation.
 
• The angular velocity is a measure of the rate of rotation of a body about a given axis and is denoted as **ω (omega)**.
 
• For a rigid body, the angular velocity of all particles is **the same** because they rotate together about the same axis at the same rate.
 
• While the linear velocity of particles depends on their distance from the axis of rotation, the angular velocity remains **constant** for all particles of the rigid body.
 
• This uniformity of angular velocity ensures that the body remains rigid and its shape does not change during rotation.
 
• Angular velocity is a **vector quantity**, having both magnitude and direction, where the direction is determined by the right-hand rule.
 
• The concept of angular velocity is widely used in **mechanics, engineering, and physics** to study rotational motion.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Proportional to its distance from the axis**__

 __
 
• The linear velocity of a particle in a rigid body is **proportional to its distance** from the axis of rotation. However, angular velocity is the same for all particles.
 
• This is because linear velocity (v) is calculated as v = ω × r, where **r** is the distance from the axis, and ω is the angular velocity.
 
 
 
• **Inversely proportional to its distance from the axis**__
 __
 
• This statement is incorrect because angular velocity does not depend on the distance from the axis. However, other properties, like torque, can depend inversely on certain factors.
 
 
 
• **Always zero**__
 
 
• For a rigid body in rotational motion, angular velocity is never zero unless the body is at rest.
 
• If angular velocity were zero, the body would not exhibit any rotational motion.

questions.question: The Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam (BSA) places emphasis on the use of technology to ensure the authenticity of evidence. This is particularly relevant for:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Digital and electronic evidence**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The **Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam (BSA)**, or the Indian Evidence Act, emphasizes the importance of using technology to ensure the **authenticity and reliability of evidence**.
 
• It is particularly relevant for **digital and electronic evidence**, as such evidence can be tampered with or altered without proper mechanisms to ensure its integrity.
 
• **Digital evidence** includes data obtained from electronic devices such as computers, smartphones, hard drives, and cloud-based storage systems. Examples include emails, SMS messages, call logs, and CCTV footage.
 
• The Act includes provisions for the **admissibility of electronic records** under Section 65B of the Indian Evidence Act, 1872, where certified electronic records are treated as evidence in courts.
 
• This emphasis on technology aligns with global judicial trends where digital evidence plays a **crucial role in solving crimes** ranging from cybercrimes to financial fraud and organized crime.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Digital and Electronic Evidence:**

 
 
• It includes all forms of evidence that are stored or transmitted in a digital format. Examples: emails, social media posts, digital documents, and server logs.
 
• Key features: It is highly prone to tampering, requires proper authentication, and necessitates the use of advanced forensic techniques for validation.
 
• Under **Section 65B of the Indian Evidence Act**, electronic records are treated as valid evidence if they meet certain technical criteria, like certification by a responsible official.
 
 
 
• **Physical Exhibits:**
 
 
• This refers to tangible objects obtained from crime scenes, such as weapons, clothing, or fingerprints.
 
• Physical evidence is crucial but is not typically subject to the same scrutiny as digital evidence in terms of authenticity checks because of its material nature.
 
 
 
• **Hand-Written Diaries:**
 
 
• This type of evidence is considered under traditional documentary evidence and does not involve technology for validation.
 
• Handwriting experts may be used for authentication.
 
 
 
• **Oral Confessions:**
 
 
• These are verbal statements made by a suspect or accused during interrogation.
 
• Such evidence is admissible under Indian law but must be corroborated with other evidence to ensure reliability.
 
 
 
• **Admissibility of Digital Evidence Globally:**
 
 
• The United Nations Office on Drugs and Crime (UNODC) has emphasized the importance of digital evidence in combating transnational crimes.
 
• Countries like the USA and the UK also have laws in place, such as the Federal Rules of Evidence in the USA, that govern the admissibility of digital evidence.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Section 65B Certification:** A certificate is required for the admissibility of electronic records, which ensures that the evidence was generated and stored in a reliable manner.
 
• **Electronic Evidence Forensics:** Advanced forensic tools are used to extract and analyze data while maintaining its integrity.
 
• **Challenges:** The dynamic nature of digital evidence, jurisdictional issues (e.g., data stored overseas), and encryption can complicate its use in legal proceedings.
 
• **Role in Modern Crimes:** Digital evidence is indispensable in solving cybercrimes, financial fraud, and even traditional crimes where technology plays a role, such as using CCTV footage in robbery cases.
 
• **Judicial Precedents:** Indian courts have increasingly relied on digital evidence, with landmark cases such as **Anvar P.V. v. P.K. Basheer** (2014) setting important precedents for admissibility.

__
 
• **Cheraw**, also known as the **bamboo dance**, is one of the most famous traditional dances of **Mizoram**.
 
• The dance involves the use of **long bamboo sticks**, which are held horizontally and tapped rhythmically on the ground by performers.
 
• The performers (usually women) move gracefully in and out of the bamboo sticks to the beat of the music without getting their feet caught.

questions.question: Which of the following **correctly **describes cooperative sector industries?

__
 
• **Cooperative sector industries** are those owned and managed by groups of individuals who share **common economic interests**. These groups often consist of **workers, suppliers, or consumers**.
 
• The primary objective is to ensure **mutual benefit**, where profits and losses are shared equally among all members.
 
• These industries follow the principle of **cooperation**, which promotes **economic equality** and prevents exploitation.
 
• Examples of cooperative sector industries include **milk cooperatives like Amul**, **handloom cooperatives**, and **agricultural cooperative societies**.
 
• Cooperatives play a crucial role in empowering rural areas by providing **employment**, **income stability**, and promoting **sustainable economic growth**.
 
• They also adhere to the democratic principle of **one member, one vote**, ensuring equitable decision-making.

• These industries are managed by the government for purposes like **national development**, **security**, and providing essential services.
 
• Examples include **Indian Railways**, **BHEL**, and **ONGC**.
 
 
 
• **Operated solely for export purposes**__
 __
 
• Industries that primarily focus on **exports** are often classified as **export-oriented industries**.
 
• They aim to produce goods and services for **international markets** rather than domestic consumption.
 
• Examples include industries involved in **textiles**, **pharmaceuticals**, and **IT services** catering to global demand.

• One of the key changes was the transfer of **Education** from the **State List** to the **Concurrent List**.
 
• By placing education in the **Concurrent List**, both the **Union Government** and the **State Governments** can legislate on matters related to education.
 
• This amendment was aimed at achieving a **uniform educational policy** across the country, ensuring better coordination and implementation of educational reforms.
 
• The **Concurrent List** is one of the three legislative lists under the **Seventh Schedule** of the Constitution of India. It contains subjects on which both the Union and State Governments can make laws.

questions.question: Argon is produced in Earth's crust via?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Decay of K-40**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Argon** is a noble gas and is chemically inert, making it an important element in various industrial applications.
 
• On Earth, **Argon** is primarily produced through the **radioactive decay of Potassium-40 (K-40).**
 
• **K-40**, a naturally occurring isotope of potassium, undergoes **beta decay** to form **Argon-40 (Ar-40)**.
 
• This process occurs deep within the **Earth's crust** and contributes significantly to the presence of argon in the atmosphere.
 
• The Earth's atmosphere contains approximately **0.93% argon**, making it the third most abundant gas after nitrogen and oxygen.
 
• The decay of K-40 is a **long-term geological process** and is essential for understanding the Earth's isotopic composition and age.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Volcanoes**__

 __
 
• Volcanoes release various gases, including water vapor, carbon dioxide, sulfur dioxide, and sometimes traces of argon. However, argon from volcanic eruptions is minimal compared to its production through the decay of K-40.
 
• Volcanic activity contributes more significantly to the release of greenhouse gases like **CO₂** rather than inert gases like argon.
 
 
 
• **Photosynthesis**__
 __
 
• **Photosynthesis** is a biological process performed by plants, algae, and cyanobacteria to convert sunlight, carbon dioxide, and water into glucose and oxygen.
 
• It does not involve the production of argon or any other noble gases.
 
 
 
• **Cosmic rays**__
 
 
• Cosmic rays are high-energy particles from outer space. They can interact with the Earth's atmosphere to produce isotopes like **Carbon-14**, but they do not contribute significantly to the formation of argon in the Earth's crust.

questions.question: Which of the following is true about Fundamental Rights and DPSPs?

options.text: Both are justiciable and enforceable by courts
DPSPs override Fundamental Rights when in conflict
Fundamental Rights are justiciable, but DPSPs are not
DPSPs are guaranteed by the Constitution;Fundamental Rights are optional

questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**Fundamental Rights are justiciable, but DPSPs are not**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Fundamental Rights** are explicitly mentioned in Part III of the **Indian Constitution**.
 
• They are enforceable by the courts, meaning individuals can approach the courts if their rights are violated. This makes them **justiciable**.
 
• The **Directive Principles of State Policy (DPSPs)**, enshrined in Part IV of the Constitution, are not enforceable by the courts, making them **non-justiciable**.
 
• DPSPs act as guidelines for the government to achieve socio-economic goals and establish a welfare state.
 
• While **Fundamental Rights** focus on individual rights and liberties, DPSPs emphasize **collective welfare** and societal development.
 
• The **Supreme Court of India** has clarified that Fundamental Rights and DPSPs must be harmonized and not seen as conflicting entities.
 
• Examples of Fundamental Rights include the **Right to Equality** (Article 14-18) and the **Right to Freedom** (Article 19-22).
 
• Examples of DPSPs include the directive to promote **equal justice** and free legal aid (Article 39A) and to ensure **living wages** for workers (Article 43).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Both are justiciable and enforceable by courts**__

 __
 
• This option is incorrect because **only Fundamental Rights** are enforceable by courts, while DPSPs are not.
 
• DPSPs serve as principles for governance and cannot be legally upheld in courts.
 
 
 
• **DPSPs override Fundamental Rights when in conflict**__
 __
 
• The **Supreme Court** has ruled that Fundamental Rights hold a higher position in cases of conflict.
 
• However, efforts have been made to harmonize both, recognizing their complementary nature.
 
 
 
• **DPSPs are guaranteed by the Constitution; Fundamental Rights are optional**__
 
 
• This is incorrect as both Fundamental Rights and DPSPs are integral parts of the Constitution.
 
• Fundamental Rights are guaranteed and enforceable, while DPSPs are guidelines that cannot be enforced legally.
